question: When exact node adjacency is changed in both counterfactuals and realization labels are held identical, does breaking the endpoint structural-type relation class disrupt a previously frozen blind hierarchical grammar more than rewiring node identity while preserving that type relation class?

designContext.interpretiveStatus: post-result mechanistic follow-up under an unchanged frozen V8 grammar, not a fresh independent holdout replication
designContext.refinement: V1 tested literal node-identity adjacency against realization assignment. V8 rules do not encode literal node IDs; they encode structural symbols and edge descriptors. V2 therefore tests the representational level the frozen grammar can actually protect: endpoint structural-type relation class versus exact node identity.

population.laneReuseNote: holdout/control were untouched when V1 began but were opened by V1 before V2 was designed; V2 reuses them as frozen evaluation lanes and must not be described as fresh independent validation

matchedIntervention.candidateSelection: deterministic minimum SHA-256 among valid candidates
edgePairCriteria: both canonical degree-preserving two-edge rewires create nonduplicate non-self relationships
exactly one rewire preserves the selected typed-edge signature and the other breaks it
matchedIntervention.typedEdgeSignature: multiset over the two selected edges of (complete edge label, unordered endpoint terminal-symbol pair)
matchedIntervention.identityRewire: change exact node adjacency while preserving the selected typed-edge signature
matchedIntervention.typeBreakingRewire: change exact node adjacency while changing the selected typed-edge signature

outcome.instrument: frozen V8 grammar; no rule refit, reordering, or selection
outcome.primaryPerObservation: hierarchical typed selective penalty = hierarchicalDataBits(typeBreakingRewire) - hierarchicalDataBits(identityRewire)
outcome.normalizedPrimary: primary typed selective penalty divided by max(1, hierarchicalDataBits(original))
outcome.positiveMeaning: breaking the endpoint structural-type relation class is less compatible with the frozen grammar than changing exact node identity while preserving that relation class
outcome.flatComparator: same typed selective penalty under the frozen V8 flat dictionary
outcome.topologyReplication: same typed selective penalty under the frozen topology-only hierarchical grammar

null.test: deterministic sign flips of each observation's normalized primary typed selective penalty within lane

adjudication.TYPED_RELATION_CLASS_SUPPORTED: all holdout and control support, sign, fraction, and sign-flip gates pass
adjudication.TYPED_RELATION_CLASS_NOT_DISTINGUISHED: support is sufficient but at least one preregistered gate fails; do not rescue by redefining type, relation, realization, or grammar after the result
adjudication.INFEASIBLE: either primary lane has fewer than its frozen minimum eligible matched interventions

falsifier: If a matched type-breaking rewire does not damage frozen evaluation-lane grammar fit more than an exact-identity rewire that preserves the same endpoint structural-type relation inventory in both reused V1 evaluation lanes, this experiment does not support the claim that V8 protects typed relationship classes beyond node identity.
claimBoundary: A pass would support the narrower mechanistic claim, on the reused V1 evaluation lanes under the unchanged frozen blind V8 grammar, that V8 protects relations among structural symbol classes rather than literal node identities. Because V2 was designed after V1 opened those lanes, a pass is not fresh independent holdout confirmation. It would not establish historical semantics, conscious machine encoding, universality, or that the terminal classes are the final functional ontology.
